issues.body: `read_varint` uses `payload.checked_shl(7 * i)`, but `checked_shl` only validates the shift count; it does not reject value bits shifted past `u64`. At `i == 9`, only payload 0 or 1 fits. A terminal byte such as `0x02` is shifted by 63 and its overflowing bit is discarded, yet the decoder accepts it because the payload is nonzero. Consequently an overflowing ten-byte encoding can decode to the same value as another encoding, contrary to the public fail-closed and canonical-encoding contract. The current tests cover a redundant-zero encoding but not this overflow boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Before combining the tenth group, reject `i == 9 && payload > 1` (or use checked multiplication/addition that detects value overflow). Add regression tests for terminal payload `0x02` and `0x7f` after nine continuation groups, and retain a positive test for the maximal canonical `u64` encoding ending in `0x01`.
issues.title: Ten-byte varints can overflow u64 and alias valid values

verdict.summary: The external-key table codec is generally careful and the conformance tests exercise real parser paths, but the unsigned-varint decoder does not actually enforce its documented 64-bit overflow invariant. A ten-byte multihash varint with a terminal payload greater than 1 is accepted after high bits are silently discarded, allowing non-canonical/overflowing encodings to alias valid codes or lengths. This is a correctness and fail-closed security defect in the public parser and needs a focused regression test and overflow check before approval.
